statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes
\[
\begin{matrix}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{matrix}
\]
where $f$ and $g$ are *Tor-independent*, meaning the higher Tor sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal O_{Y'}$ over $\mathcal O_Y$ vanish. Write $a=a_f$ and $a'=a_{f'}$ for the respective right adjoints of derived pushforward. The usual derived base-change map is $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*L(g')^*$; under Tor-independence it is an isomorphism. Its adjoint mate is the isomorphism $\xi:Rg'_*a'\xrightarrow{\sim} a Rg_*$. The duality base-change map is the natural transformation $\alpha:L(g')^*a\to a' Lg^*$ obtained by composing unit $\mathrm{id}\to Rg_*Lg^*$, $\xi^{-1}$, and counit $L(g')^*Rg'_*\to\mathrm{id}$. For each $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ let $\operatorname{Tr}_{f,K}:Rf_*a(K)\to K$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{f',Lg^*K}:Rf'_*a'(Lg^*K)\to Lg^*K$ be adjunction counits. Then the following two maps from $Lg^*Rf_*a(K)$ to $Lg^*K$ coincide:
\[
Lg^*(\operatorname{Tr}_{f,K})
\quad\text{and}\quad
Lg^*Rf_*a(K)\xrightarrow{\beta_{a(K)}}Rf'_*L(g')^*a(K)
\xrightarrow{Rf'_*(\alpha_K)}Rf'_*a'(Lg^*K)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}_{f',Lg^*K}}Lg^*K.
\]
Thus the counit/trace is compatible with Tor-independent base change.
hypotheses: Cartesian Tor-independent qcqs square; β ordinary derived pushforward base change and α its right-adjoint duality base change.
conclusions: The two natural counit/trace paths coincide.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-trace-map-and-base-change}
Suppose we have a diagram (\ref{equation-base-change}) where $f$ and $g$
are tor independent. Then the maps
$1 \star \text{Tr}_f : Lg^* \circ Rf_* \circ a \to Lg^*$ and
$\text{Tr}_{f'} \star 1 : Rf'_* \circ a' \circ Lg^* \to Lg^*$
agree via the base change maps
$\beta : Lg^* \circ Rf_* \to Rf'_* \circ L(g')^*$
(Cohomology, Remark \ref{cohomology-remark-base-change})
and $\alpha : L(g')^* \circ a \to a' \circ Lg^*$
(\ref{equation-base-change-map}).
More precisely, the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
Lg^* \circ Rf_* \circ a
\ar[d]_{\beta \star 1} \ar[r]_-{1 \star \text{Tr}_f} &
Lg^* \\
Rf'_* \circ L(g')^* \circ a \ar[r]^{1 \star \alpha} &
Rf'_* \circ a' \circ Lg^* \ar[u]_{\text{Tr}_{f'} \star 1}
}
$$
of transformations of functors commutes.

\[
L(g')^*E\xrightarrow{L(g')^*\eta_{f,E}}L(g')^*a(Rf_*E)
\xrightarrow{\alpha_{Rf_*E}}a'(Lg^*Rf_*E)
\]

\[
L(g')^*E\xrightarrow{\eta_{f',L(g')^*E}}a'(Rf'_*L(g')^*E)
\xrightarrow{a'(\beta_E^{-1})}a'(Lg^*Rf_*E).
\]

conclusions: The two unit transformations agree after base-change identifications.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-unit-and-base-change}
Suppose we have a diagram (\ref{equation-base-change}) where $f$ and $g$
are tor independent. Then the maps
$1 \star \eta_f : L(g')^* \to L(g')^* \circ a \circ Rf_*$ and
$\eta_{f'} \star 1 : L(g')^* \to a' \circ Rf'_* \circ L(g')^*$
agree via the base change maps
$\beta : Lg^* \circ Rf_* \to Rf'_* \circ L(g')^*$
(Cohomology, Remark \ref{cohomology-remark-base-change})
and $\alpha : L(g')^* \circ a \to a' \circ Lg^*$
(\ref{equation-base-change-map}).
More precisely, the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
L(g')^* \ar[r]_-{1 \star \eta_f} \ar[d]_{\eta_{f'} \star 1} &
L(g')^* \circ a \circ Rf_* \ar[d]^\alpha \\
a' \circ Rf'_* \circ L(g')^* &
a' \circ Lg^* \circ Rf_* \ar[l]_-\beta
}
$$
of transformations of functors commutes.
